open_obligations: Check that Smit et al.'s SoM uses the same number of agents and rounds as Du et al.
Note the optional summarisation step in Smit et al.
Check prompts for differences that could explain different results.
out.other_title: Multiagent debate procedure: agents read others' answers and update over rounds
out.rationale: Du et al. define multiagent debate: each agent answers, then repeatedly reads others' answers via a consensus prompt and updates. Smit et al. describe Society of Minds, which they attribute to Du et al. ('Society of Minds (SoM) Du et al. (2023) propose a MAD approach'), as agents giving answers to each other over rounds, optionally summarised, so their SoM description relies on Du et al.'s procedure.
out.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: the Society of Minds protocol as Smit et al. describe it

text: The authors describe Society of Minds (SoM, from Du et al.) as several agents giving their answers to each other over rounds, optionally summarized before being added to the shared history. They describe Multi-Persona (from Liang et al.) as an affirmative 'angel' and negative 'devil' agent each answering to a judge agent that manages the process, obtains the final solution and may end the debate early.
title: Debate protocols compared: Society of Minds and Multi-Persona (angel, devil, judge)
